title: Software Requirements Specification — New Requirements Chat

sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction
sections.body:
### 1.1 Purpose
This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the 'New Requirements Chat' project. The document serves as the primary reference for the development, testing, and deployment of the system, ensuring alignment with business objectives and compliance standards.

### 1.2 Scope
The system is designed to provide a centralized platform for managing operations, user information, records, appointments, staff, billing, and inventory. It supports role-based access control for multiple user types including Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient. Core functionalities include registration, scheduling, record management, billing, and reporting.

### 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
- **HMS**: Hospital Management System
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Records
- **OPD**: Outpatient Department
- **IPD**: Inpatient Department
- **PII**: Personally Identifiable Information
- **PCI-DSS**: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
- **GDPR**: General Data Protection Regulation
- **CCPA**: California Consumer Privacy Act

### 1.4 References
- IEEE 830-1998: IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications
- PCI-DSS v4.0
- GDPR/CCPA Compliance Guidelines

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body:
### 2.1 Product Perspective
The system operates as a standalone enterprise application with modular components for Authentication, Patients, Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, Laboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration. It integrates with external payment gateways and cloud/on-premise infrastructure.

### 2.2 User Classes and Characteristics
- **Admin**: Full system access, configuration, and audit oversight.
- **Doctor**: Clinical dashboards, diagnosis, prescriptions, and patient records.
- **Nurse**: Nursing notes, vital signs, and patient care tasks.
- **Receptionist**: Patient registration, appointment scheduling, and queue management.
- **Pharmacist**: Prescription processing and medicine inventory management.
- **Lab Technician**: Test requests and report generation.
- **Accountant**: Billing, payments, insurance, and expense management.
- **Patient**: Portal access for appointments, prescriptions, reports, and medical history.

### 2.3 Operating Environment
The system is deployed in a cloud or on-premise environment. It requires a modern web browser for the frontend and supports REST API interactions. The backend utilizes a microservices or modular monolith architecture.

### 2.4 Design and Implementation Constraints
- **Frontend**: React/Next.js
- **Backend**: FastAPI, Node.js, or Spring Boot
- **Database**: PostgreSQL or MySQL
- **Caching/Queues**: Redis
- **Authentication**: JWT/OAuth-based
- **Security**: HTTPS, password encryption, session management

### 2.5 Assumptions and Dependencies
- Stable network connectivity for cloud deployments.
- Integration with certified payment gateways for financial transactions.
- Availability of third-party services for notifications and reporting.

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: Implement JWT/OAuth-based authentication with role-based access control for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient.
Provide patient registration and profile management with data validation and audit logging.
Enable appointment scheduling, queue management, and doctor availability tracking.
Support electronic medical records including diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, and nursing notes.
Manage laboratory test requests and report generation with secure data handling.
Handle pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory with real-time stock updates.
Process billing and payments with insurance management, invoices, and receipts. Ensure PCI-DSS compliance for payment data.
Payment Gateway Integration Tests, Security Compliance Audit
Manage hospital expenses, staff management, and inventory/procurement with audit trails.
Provide real-time notifications for appointments, prescriptions, and system alerts.
Generate comprehensive reports with search/filtering capabilities and data export options.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### 4.1 Performance
- **Latency**: P95 checkout latency must be < 300ms per ECOMMERCE domain benchmarks.
- **Throughput**: System must support concurrent user targets with cart consistency under concurrent stock updates.
- **Scalability**: Architecture must scale horizontally to handle increased load without degradation.

### 4.2 Security
- **PCI-DSS Compliance**: All payment data must be tokenized, with zero plain-text card data retention. Webhook verification and idempotent charge safety are required.
- **GDPR/CCPA Compliance**: Customer PII must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Data retention and deletion policies must be enforced.
- **Authentication**: Secure authentication with password encryption and session management.
- **Transport Security**: All communications must use HTTPS.

### 4.3 Reliability
- **Availability**: 99.9% uptime SLA with disaster recovery benchmarks.
- **Data Integrity**: Database integrity constraints and regular backups.
- **Error Handling**: Robust error handling with detailed logging for troubleshooting.

### 4.4 Usability
- **Responsive UI**: Frontend must be responsive across devices.
- **Accessibility**: Interface must meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards.

### 4.5 Maintainability
- **Modularity**: Separate modules for each functional area to facilitate maintenance.
- **Logging**: Comprehensive audit logs for all critical operations.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements
sections.body:
### 5.1 User Interfaces
- **Web Portal**: Responsive web UI for patients, doctors, and staff.
- **Dashboards**: Role-specific dashboards for appointments, patient records, and clinical notes.
- **Search/Filtering**: Advanced search and filtering capabilities for records and reports.

### 5.2 Hardware Interfaces
- **Cloud/On-Premise Deployment**: System must support both cloud and on-premise deployment models.
- **Network**: Stable network connectivity for real-time data synchronization.

### 5.3 Software Interfaces
- **Payment Gateways**: Integration with certified payment gateways (e.g., Stripe) for secure transactions.
- **Notification Services**: Integration with third-party notification services for email/SMS alerts.
- **Database**: PostgreSQL/MySQL for primary data storage, Redis for caching/queues.

### 5.4 Communications Interfaces
- **REST APIs**: Standard RESTful APIs for client-server communication.
- **Webhooks**: Secure webhook verification for payment and notification events.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
### 6.1 System Constraints
- **Technology Stack**: React/Next.js (Frontend), FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot (Backend), PostgreSQL/MySQL (Database), Redis (Caching).
- **Deployment**: Cloud or on-premise with separate modules for each functional area.
- **Data Retention**: Compliance with GDPR/CCPA data retention policies.

### 6.2 Compliance Verification
- **PCI-DSS**: Regular audits to ensure compliance with payment card data security standards.
- **GDPR/CCPA**: Data protection impact assessments and regular compliance reviews.
- **Audit Logging**: All critical operations must be logged for audit purposes.

### 6.3 Open Items
- **Data Architecture & Schema Definitions**: Entity relationship diagrams (ERD) and JSON schema validation rules are required but currently missing.
- **SLA & Throughput Details**: Specific concurrent user targets and database connection limits need to be defined.
- **Compliance Mapping**: Formal compliance mapping for PCI-DSS and GDPR/CCPA is required.

File: A Hospital Management System.pdf
--- Page 1 ---
Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
